newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU opens full probe into Coca-Cola/Carlsberg deal.
newsitem.headline: EU opens full probe into Coca-Cola/Carlsberg deal.

text.p: The European Commission said on Friday it had opened a full probe into a proposed joint venture between Coca Cola Co and Carlsberg A/S of Denmark.

The European Union executive said in a statement that it wanted to address concerns that the venture, Coca-Cola Nordic Beverages A/S, could harm competition in the Danish and Swedish soft drink markets.

The venture will join the soft drink activities of U.S. soft drink giant Coca Cola and Danish brewery group Carlsberg first in Denmark and Sweden and eventually in the whole of the Nordic and Baltic regions, the Commission said.
It also involves licence agreements and a distribution joint venture with the Swedish brewer Falcon, which is jointly owned by Carlsberg and the Finnish brewing company Sinebrychoff, it said.

The Commission noted that the two parties held 60 percent of the Danish cola market, more than 40 percent of the Danish market for non-cola soft drinks and more than 70 percent of the Swedish cola market.

"Given in particular the high market shares, the Commission cannot exclude at this stage that the operation will lead to the strengthening of a dominant position in the Danish cola market, and the creation of a dominant position in the Danish market for non-cola soft drinks," it said.
"Furthermore, it seems that a dominant position could be reinforced in the Swedish cola market."
The Commission made a decision to open a detailed investigation after conducting a routine one-month probe into the venture. It now has four months to give a final ruling.
Carlsberg officials were not available for comment.
